sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Louisiana, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Friday, October 30Passed

Your request must reach your parish Registrar of Voters by 4:30 p.m. on the 4th day before the election: Friday, October 30, 2026. Military and overseas voters, and voters in the hospital, have until 4:30 p.m. the day before the election (Monday, November 2, 2026). The state suggests applying as soon as possible, because the ballot has to travel by mail both ways. (official page)

Send it back by

Monday, November 2Passed

Your voted ballot must be received by your parish Registrar of Voters by 4:30 p.m. on the day before Election Day: Monday, November 2, 2026. A postmark is not enough. Military and overseas voters, and voters in the hospital, have until 8 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Tuesday, October 27, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Louisiana’s own site

At school away from home, in Louisiana or in another state? What Louisiana says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

Yes. In Louisiana you need one of the reasons the law lists to vote by mail, unless you are a military or overseas voter. Reasons include: you will be outside Louisiana or your parish during early voting and on Election Day; you are a student, instructor or professor living outside the parish where you are registered (or the spouse or dependent of one); you work offshore; you are 65 or older; you have a disability; you are a member of the clergy assigned outside your parish; you moved more than 100 miles away after registration closed; you are in the hospital; you are a sequestered juror; or you are in jail and not serving a felony sentence. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Log in to the Louisiana Voter Portal with "Search By Voter" (your name, ZIP code and birth month and year), then choose "Request Absentee Ballot" under Quick Links. You must be logged in as the voter the ballot is for. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Print the application that fits you (for example the General Application, or the Senior Citizen Application if you are 65 or older) and send it to your parish Registrar of Voters by U.S. mail, a delivery company or fax. You list the election dates you want a ballot for on the application. Open it (official page)
  • In person. You can hand deliver the printed application to your parish Registrar of Voters. If it is handed in or faxed, it can only be for you or someone in your immediate family. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it (or send it by a delivery company) to your parish Registrar of Voters in the return envelope that comes with the ballot. (official page)
  • In person. You or a member of your immediate family can hand deliver it to the Registrar of Voters. Anyone other than you must sign a statement saying how they are related to you, and no one outside your immediate family may hand in more than one voted ballot per election. Louisiana's pages do not describe drop boxes. (official page)

What the envelope needs

On the back of the certificate envelope you sign, write your mother's maiden name (or "unknown"), and have a witness sign, print their name and write their address. If your signature, the witness's signature or your mother's maiden name is missing, the Registrar mails you a notice (and calls or emails if it has your number or address); you then go to the Registrar's office by 4:30 p.m. the day before the election to fix it, or ask for a replacement ballot. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Louisiana’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Tuesday, October 20, 2026 to Tuesday, October 27, 2026.

Anyone can vote early in person, no reason needed. For the November 3, 2026 election, early voting is October 20 to 27 (not Sunday, October 25), 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m., at the places your parish names. Bring a photo ID, or sign a voter affidavit if you do not have one. (official page)

Students

At school in Louisiana, away from home

A student living outside the parish where they are registered can ask for a ballot by mail under the "Higher Education" reason, using the General Application. If you are a student voting for the first time, you must print and mail your application with a copy of your student ID or fee bill. The state's pages do not speak separately to which address a student should register at; they say voters vote where they reside. (official page)

At school in another state, with Louisiana as home

The same "Higher Education" reason covers a Louisiana voter going to school outside their parish, including outside the state: apply with the General Application, and if you are voting for the first time, mail it with a copy of your student ID or fee bill. The state's pages do not speak to out-of-state students' residence separately. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military members, their dependents and Louisiana citizens living outside the U.S. do not need a reason. Ask on the Voter Portal, or mail, fax or email the Military or Overseas Application to your parish Registrar of Voters, or use the federal FPCA (good for at least a year). You may choose to get your ballot by email. Requests must arrive by 4:30 p.m. the day before the election (November 2, 2026), and voted ballots by 8 p.m. on Election Day (November 3, 2026). You can track your request and ballot on the Voter Portal under "Ballot Information". The federal write-in ballot (FWAB) can be used for federal offices only. (official page)

Louisiana in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • On November 3, 2026 Louisiana holds the U.S. Senate general election and an open primary for the U.S. House. Any House runoff is on Saturday, December 12, 2026 (early voting November 28 to December 5, not Sunday, November 29). A mail ballot request lists the election dates you want, so check that the December date is on yours if you may need it.
  • Louisiana's mail-ballot return deadline is the day BEFORE Election Day for most voters (4:30 p.m. Monday, November 2, 2026), earlier than many states.
  • Returning by fax: if you will not have time to mail your ballot back, you can ask your Registrar of Voters for the papers to return it by fax (a certificate and a statement giving up your right to a secret ballot). Faxed ballots have the same deadlines. Ballots cannot be returned by email unless you are a military or overseas voter allowed to during a declared emergency.
  • The state writes its 4:30 p.m. deadlines as "CST" (Central time).

How this was checked

  • The Federal Voting Assistance Program page loads by script and could not be read; it is linked, not quoted.
